fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestShipCheckStabilityRecord|TestFlakyTestBugs|TestTrimFailureLog' shows: a rerun-green head whose failed log has '--- FAIL: TestFoo' and '--- FAIL: TestScripts/bar' recorded with flakes TestFoo and TestScripts/bar and no infra entry; a rerun-green head whose log names only 'scripts (4/4) / UNKNOWN STEP' (or no job/step at all) recorded with that job / step (or 'CI run <id>') as infra and no flake; a head still red after its rerun recorded red with neither; an existing record whose flakes hold only 'job / step' entries read as infra; the watchdog queuing a bug for TestFoo and none for an infra-only run
fields.statement: When rhiza ship check settles a head that went red and then passed on a rerun, it records a flake in the CI stability record only against each failing test the failed log names (go test '--- FAIL: <name>' lines, subtests by their full name), and records a failure that names no test (only 'job / step', 'UNKNOWN STEP' or 'CI run <id>') as an infra failure kept apart from flakes, for which the watchdog files no flaky-test bug

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestCIStability|TestShipLocalGate' shows: one flake of TestX in the window stable, with a reason saying TestX was seen once and ignored, and ship gate skipping with that reason; TestX flaked on the same head twice stable; TestX and TestY flaked once each stable; TestX flaked on 2 distinct heads unstable, the reason naming TestX, its count 2 and the right N for the default window of 20 and for rhiza.ship.ciWindow=5, and stable again after N more clean runs; a window holding only infra failures stable, its reason naming them as ignored infra; a red main result unstable with no flake, and stable after a green ship check --main
fields.statement: Rhiza judges a repo's CI unstable only while one named test was recorded as a flake on at least 2 distinct heads (main or run PR) within the last rhiza.ship.ciWindow completed CI runs, or while main's latest result is red; the unstable reason names each such test, its flake count in the window and when it stops applying (after N more completed CI runs, N being the runs until the older of its two latest flakes leaves the window), and a stable verdict whose window holds infra failures or single flakes says they were seen and ignored, as does ship gate's skip reason

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestHealthCI shows a record with one 'scripts (4/4) / UNKNOWN STEP' infra failure and one single flake of TestX: the part ok (stable), listing the infra failure with count 1 and TestX with count 1 as ignored; a record where TestX flaked on 2 heads: the part warn, naming TestX, its count and when it stops applying; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/health-ci passes with the infra line in rhiza health and health --json
fields.statement: rhiza health's CI part lists, apart from the flaky tests and their counts, the infra failures in the window with their count per job / step, and states plainly that they do not make CI unstable

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestShipGateRunLog|TestShipRebase' shows: with RHIZA_RUN set, a failing gate whose output is over 64 KB with '--- FAIL: TestX' near its start and make's error lines at its end writes a log in the run's directory holding every byte, the response's log field names it, and the last 20 lines of the human output contain '--- FAIL: TestX' and 'Full log: <path>'; a second gate run in the same run writes a second file and leaves the first intact; a passing gate also writes its log; with no RHIZA_RUN the log is rhiza/gate/<branch>.log under the git common dir; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestRunStatus (or the step-journal test touched) shows a failed gate step's journal detail naming the log path; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/describe-golden passes after regenerating it for the new field; go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow passes; grep -c 'run `rhiza ship gate` to see' internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml .rhiza/workflows/ship-change.toml prints 0 for both and each gate-fix prompt names the full gate log; make self-check passes
fields.statement: Each local gate run (rhiza ship gate, and the gate ship rebase runs on a merged head) writes its whole combined output to its own log file in the run's directory, never overwriting an earlier gate log of that run (outside a run, rhiza/gate/<branch>.log under the git common dir); ShipGateResponse's log field and the gate step's journal entry carry the path, a failing gate's human output ends with its failing test lines (go test '--- FAIL:', 'FAIL', 'panic:', at most 10) and 'Full log: <path>', and the gate-fix prompts tell the fixer to read that log instead of rerunning the gate
